I usually share outdoor information, focusing on mountain climbing and drone footage.
Among the mountains I have climbed so far,
I feel there are few others where
such "accessibility" and "terror"
coexist side-by-side.
Climbing the Nishiguro Ridge of Mt. Tanigawa, one of the steepest climbing routes in the Kanto region｜minolu
Climbing the Nishiguro Ridge of Mt. Tanigawa, one of the steepest climbing routes in the Kanto region

Mt. Tanigawa is popular and has a ropeway, so it can be climbed casually. However, it is a mountain with many faces, featuring the Nishiguro Ridge route, known as one of the three steepest climbs in the Kanto region, as well as more dangerous rock areas like Ichinokurasawa.

I started trail running with the goal of completing the Mt. Fuji Mountain Race, so I was looking for a steep route that would simulate the climb from the 5th station of Mt. Fuji and ended up at the Nishiguro Ridge of Mt. Tanigawa.

From the 5th station of Mt. Fuji to the summit, you climb about 1,500 meters over a distance of about 6 kilometers. The Nishiguro Ridge of Mt. Tanigawa, by my measurement, was 10.4 kilometers with an ascent of 1,623 meters. In terms of steepness, Mt. Fuji is steeper, but it was a good place to start for my first practice.
The nearest station to Mt. Tanigawa is Doai Station.
Coming from the Kanto side, the station platform is deep underground. It is said to be called the 'Mole Station' because you have to climb 462 steps before you can even exit the station.
This alone is exhausting.
[Tanigawa Range] Mt. Tairappyo (Mt. Matsute) | A mountain trip of winter sunshine, gusty ridges, and lessons learned from a decision to retreat｜HiRO｜稜線を歩く
[Tanigawa Range] Mt. Tairappyo (Mt. Matsute) | A mountain trip of winter sunshine, gusty ridges, and lessons learned from a decision to retreat
Mt. Tairappyo is a mountain known for its excellent views and gentle ridge walking, even within the Tanigawa Range.
This time, I aimed for the timing just before the shift to a winter-type pressure pattern and entered via the Mt. Matsute route.
I was blessed with visibility that allowed me to see as far as Mt. Naeba and Mt. Fuji, but on the ridge, I encountered stronger winds than I had imagined.
As a result, I made the decision to retreat just before the summit, but it
became a mountain trip packed with lessons on the importance of judgment in winter mountains and equipment selection
I have summarized the course conditions and points of caution for the winter Mt. Tairappyo (Mt. Matsute route), as well as the "decision not to go."

[A Quick Trip to the Mountains♪] Gunma/Niigata | Rainy 'Mount Tanigawa' (One of the 100 Famous Mountains) October 2025
Since I'm not exactly 'climbing the ladder' at work, I figure I might as well raise my altitude and heart rate instead! That's the vibe I'm going for as I hike along at a relaxed pace.
The mountain I'm climbing today is 'Mt. Tanigawa,' which towers over the border between Gunma and Niigata Prefectures♪

With its twin peaks, 'Toma-no-mimi' and 'Oki-no-mimi,' it's a popular mountain that attracts many hikers because, despite its elevation of 1977m, it offers views comparable to 3000m-class peaks. Of course, it's also a famous peak listed among the '100 Famous Mountains'♪
Unfortunately, it was foggy, so there was no view at all from near the summit, but when I saw the stone cairn marker floating in the mist, it was so ethereal that all my fatigue just vanished♪
Let's get climbing right away!
